patients.summary: Healthy 21-year-old biology student with spring allergic rhinitis who joins the practice in September 2025 with a years-long recurring elbow rash. Dermatology diagnoses atopic dermatitis in November 2025 and steps up to triamcinolone in July 2026; both letters reach the practice late.

documents.title: New Patient Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 21 y/o college student, home for the summer, heading back for junior year. Parents' PPO. Has not had a regular doctor since he aged out of his pediatrician. Mentions spring allergies and "a rash on my elbows that won't quit." Membership agreement emailed. New patient physical scheduled 9/10 at 9:00 (before his afternoon lab section). Asked him to bring his vaccine card and list of OTC meds. Records release for pediatric office sent with the welcome packet.

orders.reason: Recurrent pruritic rash of antecubital fossae

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 y/o M establishing care. Junior at the university, biology. Last saw a doctor for a sports physical in high school.

CONCERNS
1. Rash, both inner elbows, on and off "for years, maybe since middle school." Itches, he scratches it raw at night sometimes. Flares some seasons more than others and seems worse right after showers. Has tried a few drugstore creams (can't recall names), they take the edge off but don't clear it. No fever, no weight loss, nothing new he's been taking.
2. Spring allergies: sneezing, stuffy nose April-June. Uses cetirizine 10 mg as needed in season and fluticasone nasal 2 sprays each side daily in spring. Fine right now.

PMH: seasonal allergic rhinitis.
PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: cetirizine prn (seasonal), fluticasone nasal (spring).
Allergies: tree/grass pollen, dust mites. NKDA.
FH: Mom had eczema as a kid. Dad has hay fever and asthma. Younger brother gets seasonal allergies.
SH: lives in an off-campus apartment with two roommates during the year, at his parents' in summer. Never smoked, never vaped. Couple of drinks on a weekend night, not every weekend. No drug use.

ROS otherwise negative.

EXAM
Vitals as charted. Well appearing.
HEENT: TMs clear. Nasal turbinates pink, not boggy today. Oropharynx clear.
Neck: supple, no nodes, thyroid not enlarged.
Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze.
Abd soft, nontender.
Skin: red patches in both antecubital fossae with linear scratch marks and some thickening of the skin. No weeping, no crusting, not tender. No similar areas elsewhere that I see.
Neuro grossly intact.

A/P
- Recurrent itchy rash, antecubital fossae, longstanding. Looks eczematous to me, and with his family history atopy is the leading thought, but it has never been formally evaluated. Referred to dermatology. Fragrance-free moisturizer in the meantime.
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis: stable, keep current regimen.
- Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids. HIV and hep C screening once, he agreed. PHQ-2 0. Childhood/adolescent vaccines per pediatric records being requested; flu and COVID when the fall supply comes in.
- Physical next September.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Logan, your blood work from yesterday is all normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar, and cholesterol. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. The dermatology referral went out this morning; their office should reach out to schedule. If you haven't heard in two weeks, let us know.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after class for vaccines. Feeling well, no fever. Screening questions negative. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM to the left arm; 2025-26 COVID vaccine IM to the right arm. Stayed 15 min, tolerated both. Pediatric records arrived last week: childhood series complete, Tdap, HPV and meningococcal doses given in adolescence. Pt asked about his dermatology appointment; it is set for November 3.
